title: What If Every Diatom in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if one invisible glass-shelled creature vanished? You would feel it with every breath.
Diatoms are algae in tiny glass shells, between 10 and 200 microns wide. About 20,000 species float in the sea.
By some estimates they make about a fifth of the oxygen produced on Earth each year.
They also pull 10 to 20 billion tonnes of carbon out of the water every year, and all of it would stop.
Their glass shells even carry silica dust to the Amazon, about 27 million tons a year.
Estimates vary, but the point holds: algae too small to see help keep the whole planet breathing.
